words.meaning: The version of the world you carry in your head. Like a map of a city: useful, but not the city itself.
How your mind copes: it keeps some things and drops others. Like hearing only your name in a noisy room.

entries.title: The Presuppositions of NLP
entries.what: The basic working beliefs of NLP. You act as if they are true because they are useful.
entries.gives: They set the attitude for every technique that follows.
entries.pic: A house on a foundation: the beliefs everything else is built on.

steps.t: Learn the main presuppositions, one at a time.
The map is not the territory: your picture of the world is not the world itself.
There is no failure, only feedback: every result teaches you something.
The meaning of communication is the response you get: judge your message by how it lands.
Every behaviour has a positive intention: behind every action is a good reason.
People already have the resources they need, or can build them.
If one thing does not work, do something different.
Choose one presupposition each week and act as if it is true.

words.meaning: Something you take as true in order to start, like the rules of a game.
Information about what happened, used to do better next time.

entries.title: Calibration
entries.what: Noticing small changes in a person's face, skin and breathing.
entries.gives: You see how a person feels, often before they say it.
entries.pic: An eye watching closely for small changes.

steps.t: Watch the person when they are calm. This is their normal.
Choose one thing to watch: breathing, skin colour or lips.
Talk about something they like.
Then talk about something they dislike.
Notice what changes compared with their normal.
Do not guess what it means. Only notice the change.
Practise one signal a day for a week.
